hints.title: Subsequence Length Constraint
hints.text: Any subsequence containing at least m elements has its first element at index i and last at index j with j minus i at least m minus 1.

hints.title: Prefix Extremes Tracking
hints.text: Maintain both the minimum and maximum values encountered in the valid prefix up to index j minus m plus 1.

hints.title: Sign Consideration for Products
hints.text: Multiplying by a negative number can yield a maximal product with the minimum prefix value.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxProduct(self, nums: List[int], m: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        if n < m:
            return 0
        
        pref_min = float('inf')
        pref_max = -float('inf')
        best = -float('inf')
        
        for j in range(m - 1, n):
            i = j - (m - 1)
            pref_min = min(pref_min, nums[i])
            pref_max = max(pref_max, nums[i])
            
            val = nums[j]
            best = max(best, val * pref_min, val * pref_max)
            
        return best
```

complexity.notes: Single pass tracking running prefix minimum and maximum.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all pairs of indices requires O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Updating rolling minimum and maximum avoids extra storage beyond scalar variables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Track both minimum and maximum to account for negative products.
